turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I noticed a mass in my left breast about four weeks ago, and it has been rapidly getting bigger. I haven’t had any pain, and I haven’t noticed any skin or nipple changes.
How old are you?
Patient: I’m 48 years old.
Do you have any personal or family history of breast cancer or other cancers?
Patient: I don’t have any personal history of breast cancer or other cancers, and there’s no family history of breast cancer.
Are you currently pre‑menopausal, peri‑menopausal, or post‑menopausal? If you’re still having periods, have they changed recently?

Patient: I’m peri-menopausal—my periods have become a bit irregular over the past several months, but I’m not fully done with them yet. I haven’t noticed a sudden change in flow right around when the mass started.
Has the mass felt firm or soft, and is it movable or fixed to the underlying tissue or skin?
Patient: It feels firm to me, and it doesn’t seem very movable—it feels kind of fixed in the underlying tissue rather than shifting around.
Do you feel any swelling or lumps in the armpit on the same side as the breast mass?
Patient: Yes, I think I may have noticed a small lump in my left armpit too, but I’m not totally sure if it’s swelling or just enlarged tissue.
Have you noticed any nipple discharge from either breast? If so
I haven’t noticed any nipple discharge from either breast. I also haven’t had any skin changes over the mass, and it isn’t painful.
Have you experienced any unexplained weight loss, fevers, night sweats, or fatigue over the past few weeks?
Patient: No—I haven’t had any unexplained weight loss, fevers, night sweats, or unusual fatigue. I’ve generally been feeling like myself aside from noticing the mass growing.
Are you currently taking or have you recently taken hormone replacement therapy, oral contraceptives, or any other hormonal medications?
Patient: I’m not taking hormone replacement therapy, oral contraceptives, or any hormonal medications. I haven’t started anything new around the time I noticed the mass.
Do you see any dimpling, puckering, or retraction of the skin over the mass, or any ulceration?
Patient: I haven’t noticed any dimpling, puckering, or retraction of the skin over the mass, and there’s been no ulceration.
Approximately how large does the lump feel? (You
Patient: I think it’s gotten to about 3 to 4 centimeters in size over these four weeks, and it feels firm and rather fixed in place.
